solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deer kept out of sight crossing southern end of glen

indicators.note: the hiding word straddles the other letter, lying across it on both sides

parts.note: something kept out of sight has been hid, an old past tense of hide

indicators.note: in a down entry the southern end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A deer stays hidden as it moves across the far end of a Scottish valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts N, the last letter of 'glen', inside HID.
explanation.definitionFit: A hind is a female red deer, so the word names a kind of deer.

clue.text: Stick a note in this place

parts.note: D is one of the notes of the musical scale
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Someone told to put a memo up on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Bad-mannered male, Italian, entering bar after one

indicators.note: the rest of the letters come after the one, so it heads the answer

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the Italian abbreviation goes into the word for a bar, splitting it

parts.note: a pole is a bar or rod

explanation.surface: A rude Italian man barges into a pub just after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a rod; 'entering' signals the insertion and 'after' puts the one first.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite means lacking good manners, a direct synonym of bad-mannered.

clue.text: Foolish talk over a list

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over, above, the next

parts.note: rot is nonsense, foolish talk

explanation.surface: Nonsense spoken about a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a list of people and the turns they take for duties.

clue.text: Language used within confines of stag party

indicators.note: the language is placed inside the outer letters of the next word
the confines of a word are its boundary letters, first and last

parts.note: Hindi is a language of India

explanation.surface: Some foreign tongue gets spoken at a groom's last night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confines of' gives S and G from 'stag'; 'used within' puts HINDI between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Small amount of paper for a country gentleman

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a quire is a measure of paper, twenty-four or twenty-five sheets

explanation.surface: A few sheets of paper handed over for a rural landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire is the chief landowner of an English country district, a country gentleman.

clue.text: Beverage teenager brewed

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms its ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink a youngster has made in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges the letters of TEENAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea, an example of a beverage.

clue.text: Old politician going into price for fertiliser

indicators.note: the old politician pieces go inside the word for price

parts.note: cost means price
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A former MP's expenses go on garden fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'politician' alone gives only the MP part; 'Old' supplies its own letter, and 'going into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Compost is decayed organic matter dug into soil as a fertiliser.

clue.text: Essex Man from Harwich, a vulgarian

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A coarse type from an Essex port town is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points at the letters spanning the end of 'Harwich', 'a' and the start of 'vulgarian'. Harwich is a port in Essex, and 'Essex Man' is a British stereotype of a brash, materialistic voter.
explanation.definitionFit: The derogatory British slang word is used for a loutish working-class youth, the type caricatured as Essex Man.

clue.text: Formal agreement to take out Yemen's leader

parts.note: to take someone out for a meal is to treat them

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A peace deal agreed so that a ruler could be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take out' suggests killing, but here it means paying for an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal written agreement between states.

clue.text: Inappropriate, a French affair of honour, unconcluded

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the word loses its conclusion, its final letter

parts.note: a duel was fought to settle an affair of honour

explanation.surface: A French duel left unfinished is thought improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconcluded' cuts the L from DUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or not warranted, so unsuitable or inappropriate.

clue.text: Develop complex

definitions.meaning: to work out in more detail, as a verb
intricate, full of detail, as an adjective

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb, to expand on detail, and an adjective, intricate, matching both senses.

clue.text: To unsay what has been said about sappers is cowardly

indicators.note: the retracting word goes about, around, the sappers

parts.words: To unsay what has been said
parts.note: to recant is to retract a statement
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British army's sappers

explanation.surface: Taking back one's words in front of army engineers is seen as cowardice.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; 'about' signals that one piece wraps the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an archaic adjective meaning craven or faint-hearted.

clue.text: Measure mountain range

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length of 22 yards

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an old length unit used for cricket pitches and a linked series of peaks.

clue.text: Wager involving trouble in lodge

indicators.note: the wager word wraps round the trouble word

parts.note: a bet is a wager
ill means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: A gamble going wrong at a country lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodge' looks like a noun, a hunting lodge, but it is the verb; 'involving' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To billet soldiers is to lodge them in private houses, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Quantity of drink, low in calories, divided by right

indicators.note: the low-calorie word is split by the letter for right

parts.note: lite is the commercial spelling for low-calorie food and drink

explanation.surface: A diet drink served with the correct measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided by' puts R inside LITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of volume, a quantity in which drinks are sold.

clue.text: It's not easy providing a spread indoors?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a hard task
a meal laid out inside cannot be an outdoor meal on a blanket

explanation.surface: Laying on a buffet inside the house is tougher than it looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a difficult task, and literally an indoor spread is not an alfresco meal.

clue.text: That memento, neglected now

indicators.note: something neglected falls into disarray, so the letters are left in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A keepsake that has been forgotten lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' rearranges the letters of THAT MEMENTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means currently, at this present time, a synonym of now.

clue.text: Drink, it spilled over a girl

indicators.note: in a down entry this piece sits over the rest
spilled liquid lands out of place, so the two letters swap order

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone knocks a drink over a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' swaps the two letters of 'it' to make TI; 'over' places it above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the brand name of a coffee liqueur, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Alluring island castle

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means alluring

explanation.surface: An attractive island fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamis Castle in Scotland was the childhood home of the late Queen Mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamis is a famous Scottish castle, setting of Macbeth's thaneship.

clue.text: Determined, good man approaches English cathedral city

indicators.note: the saint comes up to, just before, the other pieces

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A resolute holy man heads toward an English cathedral town.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely describes a hard, resolute will, so firmly determined.

clue.text: Gold on country carriage

indicators.note: the gold sits on, after, the country

parts.note: a land is a country
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Gold found on a nation's horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry 'on' puts the gold after the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood.

clue.text: Where the buffalo roamed, what could provide stew?

parts.note: read the answer's first word as an anagram signal working on its second: the four letters scrambled wildly give stew

explanation.surface: Asking where bison once roamed and what would make a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, makes the clue word 'stew'.
explanation.definitionFit: The frontier region of the American West was where great herds of bison roamed.

clue.text: Told stories, on the way up, about volunteers in army unit

indicators.note: the turned word goes round the volunteers
in a down entry, going up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie, so lied
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Fibs were told rising through the ranks about reservists in a regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns LIED into DEIL, which suits a down entry; 'about' signals that it wraps the volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a small group of soldiers assigned a special task, an army unit.

clue.text: Benevolent type

definitions.meaning: a sort or class, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for generous and caring and a noun for a sort or variety.

clue.text: Russian aircraft helping movement of people?

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Soviet jets assisting the movement of a population.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Migration is the movement of people or animals from one region to another.

clue.text: Food — good spread

parts.note: a rub is a paste or mix spread on meat before cooking

explanation.surface: Food served as a decent feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for food.

clue.text: Lieutenant suffering setback in match for championship

indicators.note: the turned abbreviation goes inside the word for match

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: An officer has a reverse in the game that decides a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British knockout match; 'suffering setback' turns the abbreviation backwards, giving TL, and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a title is a championship, as in winning the league title.

clue.text: Excessively large instrument

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: A device that is far too big.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement or instrument used for a job.

clue.text: Considered duties to be sorted out by daughter

indicators.note: sorting things out puts them into a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Tasks weighed up and organised by a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' makes STUDIE from the six letters; 'to be' and 'by' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Studied means carefully considered or deliberate, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Salad ingredient for fashionable party person short of time

parts.note: chic means fashionable

indicators.note: the party member is lacking the letter for time

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A salad leaf for a trendy Conservative pressed for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes T from TORY, leaving ORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicory is a bitter leaf vegetable used in salads.
